answer: Panels are drawn from a public random beacon each epoch, so no one can choose which jurors grade their answer. A new key's vote counts for nothing until it has sealed 20 grades that matched the final verdict, so a farm of hollow keys holds no power on day one. Each key also posts a 50 POA bond; if two keys keep showing the same rare tells, like both slipping saffron into unrelated answers, a jury links them and both bonds burn. Faking 100 voters takes 2,000 verdict-matched grades of real work plus 5,000 POA at risk.
